title: Knowledge check: Express.js History and Evolution

questions.prompt: In Express.js History and Evolution, which statement best describes Origins and development?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.

Configure the origins, methods and headers required by the application rather than using an unrestricted allowlist. CORS controls browser access; it does not authenticate requests or authorize data changes.
Separate current Express 5 behavior from legacy Express 4 behavior. Confirm version-specific syntax against the migration guide and use regression tests instead of assuming compatibility.
questions.answer_key: Configure the origins, methods and headers required by the application rather than using an unrestricted allowlist. CORS controls browser access; it does not authenticate requests or authorize data changes.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Express.js History and Evolution?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
